Conditions:

If the first element is a symbol and the last a number, the codes for these two (the first and the last elements) are to be interchanged.

If the first element is an odd number and the last an even number, the first and last elements are to be coded as .

If both second and third elements are perfect squares, the third element is to be coded as the code for the second element.

Given- 3 4 9 7

The 1st element is 3 (an odd number).

The 2nd element is 4 (a perfect square).

The 3rd element is 9 (a perfect square).

The last element is 7 (an odd number).

Rule No. (1): This condition does not apply because the first element (3) is a number, not a symbol.

Rule No. (2): This condition does not apply because the last element (7) is an odd number, not an even number.

Rule No. (3): This condition applies because the second element (4) is a perfect square and the third element (9) is also a perfect square. So, the code of the third element will be the code for the second element.

Based on the applicable rule (3), the third element will be coded as the code of the second element.

The code for 3 is F.

The code for 4 is G.

The code for 9 is B.

But, due to rule (3), 9 will be coded as G (the code for 4).

The code for 7 is M.

Thus, '3 4 9 7' is coded as → F G G M.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 3".**
